svg.aria-label: Before-and-after comparison of two Money representations for QuizStakes, measured on Oracle JDK 21.0.7 on macOS aarch64 with compressed oops on. On the left, Money as a record of BigDecimal amount and Currency currency: the record itself is 24 bytes and holds a reference to a BigDecimal of 40 bytes (12-byte header plus intVal reference 4, scale 4, precision 4, stringCache reference 4 and intCompact long 8, giving 36 aligned up to 40) and a reference to a shared interned Currency that is not charged per Money, for 64 bytes per Money; one full 3.33 stake split allocates 192 bytes counted from a pre-built stake Money — four BigDecimals at 40, three Money records at 24, and a two-element array at 24 — or 256 bytes counted from a bare long, which adds one more BigDecimal at 40 and one more Money at 24. On the right, MoneyMinor as a record of a long units field and Currency: 12-byte header plus 8-byte long plus 4-byte Currency reference is exactly 24 bytes, and one full 3.33 split allocates 72 bytes counted from a pre-built stake MoneyMinor — two MoneyMinor records at 24 plus a two-element array at 24 — or 96 bytes counted from a bare long, which adds one more MoneyMinor at 24. The ratio is 2.67 times on both bases: 192 over 72, and 256 over 96. Both sides show the same split, 3.33 into 0.33 bonus plus 3.00 cash, or 333 minor units into 33 plus 300. The right side also states the overflow bound: Long.MAX_VALUE is 9,223,372,036,854,775,807 minor units, which at scale 2 is 92,233,720,368,547,758.07 major units, roughly 9.2 times ten to the sixteenth, which is why plus still needs Math.addExact rather than a bare plus operator. All byte figures are measured under the flag minus X X colon minus DoEscapeAnalysis; under the default JIT, escape analysis scalar-replaces part of the BigDecimal path and one run measured 152 bytes against 72 bytes, because with escape analysis on the long path is 72 bytes on both bases — the extra MoneyMinor that the bare-long basis adds gets scalar-replaced. That is why each panel states the basis of the count rather than a single number.
svg.text: Money two ways: a BigDecimal object graph against one minor-unit long
BEFORE — Money(BigDecimal amount, Currency currency)
Money — record, 64 B total
header 12 + amount oop 4 + currency oop 4 = 20
aligned up to 24 B for the record itself
BigDecimal.valueOf(333, 2) — 40 B
12 object header
+ 4 intVal ref (BigInteger)
+ 4 scale
+ 4 precision
+ 4 stringCache ref
+ 8 intCompact long
= 36, aligned to 40 B
Currency — interned
one shared instance per ISO code
not charged per Money
ONE 3.33 SPLIT — BigDecimal PATH
stake 3.33 → bonus 0.33, cash 3.00, sum 3.33
bonus = stake.multiply(new BigDecimal("0.10")).setScale(2, RoundingMode.DOWN)
allocations depend on where the count starts:
from a pre-built stake Money: 192 B (40 + 40 + 24 + 40 + 24 + 24)
from a bare long: 256 B (adds one BigDecimal 40 + one Money 24)
the scale travels with the value, so JPY (0) and BHD (3)
need no call-site change
64 B per Money · 192 B or 256 B per 3.33 split, by basis
measured on Oracle JDK 21.0.7, macOS aarch64, compressed oops on
NO OVERFLOW BOUND — BigDecimal IS ARBITRARY-PRECISION
intCompact carries the value in a long while it fits; past that,
intVal — a BigInteger — takes over and the object grows.
So there is no addExact discipline to remember, and no fixed cost.
That safety is what the 40 extra bytes per Money buy.
AFTER — MoneyMinor(long units, Currency currency)
MoneyMinor — record, 24 B total
header 12 + units long 8 + currency oop 4 = 24
exactly 24 B — no alignment padding needed
long units — one primitive
no object header, no oop, no
indirection: the value lives
inline in the record layout
Currency — interned
the same shared instance
as the BigDecimal form uses
not charged per MoneyMinor
ONE 3.33 SPLIT — long PATH
stake 333 minor units → bonus 33, cash 300, sum 333
allocations depend on where the count starts:
from a pre-built stake MoneyMinor: 72 B (2 x MoneyMinor 24 + array 24)
from a bare long: 96 B (adds one MoneyMinor 24)
integer division truncates toward zero — no RoundingMode argument needed
cost: scale is fixed at construction, so JPY (0) and BHD (3) move onto the caller
24 B per MoneyMinor · 72 B or 96 B per 3.33 split, by basis
192 / 72 and 256 / 96 per split — 2.67x on both bases
All byte figures are measured under -XX:-DoEscapeAnalysis. Under the default JIT, escape analysis scalar-replaces part of
the BigDecimal path — one run measured 152 B against 72 B, because with escape analysis on the long path is 72 B on both
bases: the extra MoneyMinor the bare-long basis adds gets scalar-replaced. Hence each panel states its basis.
OVERFLOW BOUND OF THE long MINOR-UNIT FORM
Long.MAX_VALUE = 9,223,372,036,854,775,807 minor units
at scale 2 that is 92,233,720,368,547,758.07 major units
≈ 9.2 × 10^16 — ample headroom at 19.8M ledger entries a day
but plus() still needs Math.addExact, never a bare + operator
the BigDecimal-backed Money and what its precision buys
the field-by-field byte arithmetic, and the long form's bound
the costlier total — 64 B per value, 192 B or 256 B per split
the minor-unit long form and its cheaper total
shared interned Currency — not charged to either form
annotation panel — the split, actually run, and its cost
record field — arrow points at the object the field holds
